meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Was Owen heard before you entered that zero?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess. Its own maker says not to punish a student on that alone. What else do you have?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Go on.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. I'm writing that down. He wrote it over the weekend somewhere else and pasted it in, and under 4.1 you were supposed to ask him that first.

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Give me the play, I'll read it myself. A wrong quotation is a seventeen-year-old copying a line off some study site. And whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet.
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
People change their argument between an outline and a final draft. That's what an outline is for. And you haven't answered me on the quotation.

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.
So you spoke to him on November 2. A boy put on the spot by his teacher for five minutes goes quiet, and those are your notes, not his words. What is it you want from him?

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.
Forty minutes in a classroom isn't a weekend at home with the play open. You keep adding paper and you haven't answered me. What do you want from him?

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.
That's 4.4. He'll sit the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. In writing tonight, nothing on his record, and the rest of my points will be in my email.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Okay. Thursday, November 12, after school, marked within two days. Put that in tonight's email as well. Ten minutes.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes. On those terms, and only those.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

You agreed today that Owen will sit a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 this Thursday, November 12, after school, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require every one of those terms in writing, along with your answers to the points I raised about the quotation, the outline, your November 2 notes and the weight you gave the checker score. You said I would have that in writing tonight, and I expect it tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, marked within two days, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record. She still wants all of it in writing tonight and her remaining points answered by email. That is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it with time left on her clock.

What moved her: you showed the version history with its times, and when she said he wrote it elsewhere and pasted it in, you invited that other document and its history. It was dated, checkable, and her one defence had an answer.

What cost ground: you opened with the checker score and said the zero stands. To her that is a machine's opinion she can't check, and it kept her at her opening position until you started over.

What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop. Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's text arriving late on a Wednesday night in October, between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM, the night before it was due, which is very close to the kind of night she has been avoiding. It proves nothing about the essay. It is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: when she said the invented quotation was a line copied off some study site, answer that before moving on to the outline. She told you outright it was unanswered, and it stayed open to the end.
